nodes.label: logcheck golangci-lint Module Plugin
nodes.rationale: make lint builds a custom golangci-lint binary with the sigs.k8s.io/logtools logcheck plugin to validate structured logging calls (balanced key-value pairs) per Kubernetes conventions.

nodes.label: Kubebuilder Project Conventions
nodes.rationale: Generated files (config/crd/bases, config/rbac/role.yaml, zz_generated.*, PROJECT) must never be hand-edited; scaffold markers must never be removed because the CLI injects code at them; files must stay in expected locations; APIs and webhooks are created via kubebuilder CLI commands, not manually.

nodes.label: Kubernetes Logging Message Conventions
nodes.rationale: Log messages start with a capital, no trailing period, active voice, past tense, object type specified, and balanced key-value pairs — machine-checkable style borrowed from upstream Kubernetes.

nodes.label: k8s-r8r Helm Chart
nodes.rationale: kubeVersion >=1.30.0-0 because the advisory validating webhook uses CEL matchConditions, GA since Kubernetes 1.30 (see docs/security.md).

nodes.label: ReplicationPolicy CRD
nodes.rationale: Cluster-scoped admin-controlled security boundary: allowlist of source kinds/namespaces and target clusters/namespaces, with options gating side effects — allowNamespaceCreation defaults false, allowedConflictPolicies defaults [Fail] because Overwrite/Adopt touch unmanaged objects (design D7), revocationPolicy defaults Delete. Designs D4/D6: controller re-evaluates authoritatively; admission checks are advisory.

nodes.label: Replication CRD
nodes.rationale: Canonical operator-owned materialization of one replication request (design D1), never authored by users. Status inventory is the source of truth for garbage collection — no code path may lose track of a created replica. NonReadyTargets is capped at 20 with an overflow counter; full per-target truth lives in metrics and events (design D8). TargetName is the only rename mechanism — automatic renaming never occurs (design D7).

nodes.label: k8s-r8r-policy-admin ClusterRole
nodes.rationale: The chart creates this persona role but never binds it — it must be bound deliberately, to cluster admins only, because ReplicationPolicy is the security boundary (default deny, allowlist-only).

nodes.label: k8s-r8r-replication-viewer ClusterRole
nodes.rationale: Users never write Replications (the operator owns them), so read-only is the full user-facing surface; the aggregation label folds these permissions into the built-in view ClusterRole.

nodes.label: vreplicationrequest ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
nodes.rationale: failurePolicy Ignore is mandatory and deliberately not a chart value: the webhook is advisory UX only — the controller re-evaluates ReplicationPolicy authoritatively on every reconcile, so a bypassed webhook can never cause unauthorized replication; Fail would let operator downtime block all annotated Secret/ConfigMap writes cluster-wide. timeoutSeconds 2 for the same reason. CEL matchConditions (GA in K8s 1.30) ensure only objects with r8r.io/ annotations incur an admission call, and removing all annotations bypasses the webhook so cleanup is always admitted. Templated from HAND-MAINTAINED config/webhook/manifests.yaml because controller-gen markers cannot express matchConditions.

nodes.label: Advisory Admission Webhook Design (D6)
nodes.rationale: Apply-time feedback that is never an availability or security dependency: sideEffects None, failurePolicy Ignore, small timeout, CEL-scoped to opted-in objects; authoritative enforcement always happens in the controller.

nodes.label: Chart Self-Signed Issuer
nodes.rationale: A self-signed issuer suffices because the webhook is advisory (failurePolicy Ignore): only the API server verifies the certificate, via the CA bundle cert-manager injects.

nodes.label: Kustomize Webhook Serving Certificate
nodes.rationale: SERVICE_NAME/SERVICE_NAMESPACE placeholders are substituted by replacements in config/default/kustomization.yaml when the [CERTMANAGER] blocks are enabled.

nodes.label: Kustomize Self-Signed Issuer
nodes.rationale: Self-signed is suitable because the webhook is advisory (failurePolicy Ignore): only the API server verifies this certificate via the injected CA bundle.

nodes.label: Issuer Name Reference Kustomize Config
nodes.rationale: Teaches kustomize how to rewrite spec/issuerRef/name inside cert-manager Certificate objects when the Issuer is renamed by namePrefix, keeping cross-object references consistent.

nodes.label: ReplicationPolicy CRD
nodes.rationale: Cluster-scoped admin-controlled security boundary. Policy is re-evaluated authoritatively on every reconcile; admission-time checks are advisory only (design D4/D6). Project RBAC restricts writes to cluster administrators.

nodes.label: Default-Deny Policy Allowlist
nodes.rationale: With no policies present nothing replicates (default deny); multiple policies combine by union. Omitted options take safe defaults: no namespace creation, conflicts Fail, revocation Delete. Kinds outside the operator's global allowlist are never replicated regardless of policy.

nodes.label: ConflictPolicy (Fail/Overwrite/Adopt)
nodes.rationale: Describes how the engine treats a pre-existing unmanaged object occupying an intended replica's name (design D7). Defaults to [Fail]; Overwrite and Adopt must be explicitly granted because they touch objects k8s-r8r does not manage.

nodes.label: RevocationPolicy (Retain/Delete)
nodes.rationale: Controls what happens to already-created replicas when a policy stops permitting them. Defaults to Delete, so revoked replicas are cleaned up rather than orphaned.

nodes.label: AllowNamespaceCreation Gate
nodes.rationale: Defaults to false: replication into a nonexistent namespace fails with a condition instead of silently creating cluster-level structure. When enabled, created namespaces are labeled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: k8s-r8r.

nodes.label: Replication CRD
nodes.rationale: Canonical, operator-owned materialization of one replication request (design D1). Lives in the source object's namespace, carries the resolved fanout in spec, reports status plus replica inventory. Users never author these directly — the annotation shim creates them; project RBAC grants users read-only access. Namespaced, with status subresource and printer columns Ready/Desired/Failed/Age.

nodes.label: Annotation Origin
nodes.rationale: Origin records which request kind materialized this Replication. Currently always Annotation (the annotation shim); the enum is designed to admit future origins such as ReplicationSet.

nodes.label: ResolvedTarget Fanout Entry
nodes.rationale: Resolution happens on the hub against discovered cluster inventory; the engine consumes these entries verbatim. TargetName is the only rename mechanism — automatic renaming never occurs (design D7), keeping renames explicit and git-visible.

nodes.label: Replica Inventory
nodes.rationale: Source of truth for garbage collection: no code path may lose track of a created replica (replication-engine spec). Drives GC on source deletion, annotation removal, target deselection, and cluster deregistration.

nodes.label: Source Hash Drift Detection
nodes.rationale: Replicas carry an r8r.io/source-hash (sha256:<hex>); lastAppliedHash is compared against watch events to detect drift without caching replica payloads on the hub.

nodes.label: NonReadyTargets Cap
nodes.rationale: Per-target detail entries are recorded only while a target is not ready, capped at 20 with NonReadyOverflow counting the rest; full per-target truth lives in metrics and events (design D8). Healthy targets never appear here, keeping status objects bounded.

nodes.label: CRD Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Not intended to run by itself since it depends on service name and namespace outside this package; should be run by config/default.

nodes.label: Cert-Manager Metrics Certs Manager Patch
nodes.rationale: JSON patch adding volumeMount, --metrics-cert-path arg, and a volume backed by the metrics-server-cert secret so the manager serves metrics with cert-manager certs.

nodes.label: metrics-server-cert Secret
nodes.rationale: cert-manager-issued secret (ca.crt/tls.crt/tls.key) shared by the manager's metrics server and the Prometheus ServiceMonitor TLS config, enabling verified end-to-end TLS for metrics scraping.

nodes.label: Default Kustomization Overlay
nodes.rationale: Top-level overlay: sets namespace k8s-r8r-system and namePrefix k8s-r8r-, composes rbac + manager + metrics service, applies the HTTPS metrics patch. CRD, webhook, cert-manager, prometheus, and network-policy sections are scaffolded but commented out (opt-in).

nodes.label: Manager HTTPS Metrics Patch
nodes.rationale: Adds --metrics-bind-address=:8443 so the metrics endpoint is exposed over HTTPS on port 8443.

nodes.label: Controller Manager Deployment
nodes.rationale: Runs /manager with --leader-elect and --health-probe-bind-address=:8081; hardened per restricted Pod Security Standards (runAsNonRoot, seccomp RuntimeDefault, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop ALL capabilities) to meet the highest Kubernetes security requirements.

nodes.label: Allow Metrics Traffic NetworkPolicy
nodes.rationale: Restricts ingress to the metrics endpoint (port 8443) to pods in namespaces labeled metrics: enabled, so only opted-in namespaces can scrape metrics.

nodes.label: Controller Manager ServiceMonitor
nodes.rationale: Scrapes /metrics over HTTPS on the 'https' port with a service-account bearer token; ships with insecureSkipVerify: true and documents that production should switch to cert-manager-managed certs via the TLS patch.

nodes.label: ServiceMonitor TLS Patch
nodes.rationale: Replaces the insecure tlsConfig with verified TLS (serverName SERVICE_NAME.SERVICE_NAMESPACE.svc substituted by kustomize) using ca.crt/tls.crt/tls.key from the cert-manager-managed metrics-server-cert secret.

nodes.label: RBAC Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Composes service account, roles, bindings, leader election, and metrics auth/reader roles; metrics auth RBAC protects the metrics endpoint with authn/authz and can be commented out to disable that protection.

nodes.label: Leader Election Role
nodes.rationale: Grants configmaps, coordination.k8s.io leases, and event creation permissions needed for controller-runtime leader election.

nodes.label: Personas Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Persona ClusterRoles are intentionally NOT included in the default overlay; operators apply or reference them explicitly (e.g. from the Helm chart) so privileges are granted deliberately.

nodes.label: k8s-r8r Policy Admin ClusterRole
nodes.rationale: Full CRUD on ReplicationPolicy. Policies are the security boundary of k8s-r8r (default deny, allowlist-only), so this role must be bound only to cluster administrators, and is never bound automatically.

nodes.label: k8s-r8r Replication Viewer ClusterRole
nodes.rationale: Read-only access to Replication objects because users never write Replications — the operator owns them — so read-only is the full user-facing surface. The aggregate-to-view label folds these permissions into the built-in view ClusterRole.

nodes.label: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
nodes.rationale: Hand-maintained (design D6): controller-gen cannot express matchConditions, so this file is excluded from make manifests regeneration and must stay in sync with internal/webhook (Path constant /validate-replication-request, handled kinds secrets/configmaps).

nodes.label: Advisory Webhook (failurePolicy Ignore)
nodes.rationale: failurePolicy Ignore is mandatory: the webhook is advisory UX only. If it is unavailable, writes must proceed — the controller re-evaluates ReplicationPolicy authoritatively on every reconcile, so a bypassed webhook can never cause unauthorized replication. Setting Fail would make operator downtime block all annotated Secret/ConfigMap writes cluster-wide. timeoutSeconds 2 for the same reason: feedback is nice-to-have, user writes must not wait.

nodes.label: CEL MatchConditions Annotation Scoping
nodes.rationale: Only objects carrying an r8r.io/ annotation reach the webhook, so ordinary Secret/ConfigMap traffic never incurs an admission call. On UPDATE the incoming object is evaluated, so removing all r8r.io annotations bypasses the webhook — cleanup is always admitted. matchConditions are GA since Kubernetes 1.30, which sets the minimum supported version.

nodes.label: Default Deny
nodes.rationale: With no policies present nothing replicates (PolicyDenied). Allowlist only — no deny rules; denying is done by not allowing. A target needs a single policy matching ALL dimensions (source namespace, source kind, target cluster, target namespace); dimensions never combine across policies, but policies union. NetworkPolicy mental model. Developers gain no new privileges: there is no mechanism to override policy from the request side.

nodes.label: ReplicationPolicy
nodes.rationale: Cluster-scoped, admin-owned allowlist evaluated authoritatively on every reconcile; the admission webhook only mirrors it for apply-time feedback. Policy-side empty clusterSelector matches ALL clusters (unlike the request-side annotation where empty selects none): requests must be explicit, policies may be broad. Invalid selectors fail closed.

nodes.label: Allowed Conflict Policies
nodes.rationale: Fail (default) reports Conflict and leaves unmanaged objects untouched; Adopt takes ownership only when content hash equals source hash; Overwrite replaces the payload and is weaponizable (could replace a victim cluster's existing secret) so it should be granted narrowly. Options union across permitting policies, Fail always included; engine acts with the strongest granted policy.

nodes.label: Revocation Policy
nodes.rationale: Delete (default) removes replicas on the next reconcile — revoked data should not linger on the fleet; Retain leaves them but stops updates and sets PolicyRevoked. Most conservative wins when policies combine. Revocation is live: policy is re-evaluated every reconcile, no grandfathering.

nodes.label: Clean Teardown Order
nodes.rationale: Order matters because the operator garbage-collects replicas only while running: remove requests (or delete policies with revocationPolicy Delete), wait for Replications to drain, then helm uninstall, optionally delete CRDs, then clean spoke bootstrap leftovers. Helm deliberately keeps crds/-installed CRDs.

nodes.label: Orphan Discovery via Labels
nodes.rationale: Orphans stay discoverable via app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=k8s-r8r and r8r.io/source-namespace / r8r.io/source-name labels on every cluster; engine-created namespaces carry the label too but are never engine-deleted.

nodes.label: EventLimiter
nodes.rationale: Engine component all repeatable event emissions must route through so a flapping target cannot flood the event stream.

nodes.label: Bounded Metric Cardinality
nodes.rationale: Metrics prefixed k8s_r8r_ on the controller-runtime metrics.Registry; labels only cluster/namespace/kind or a small closed enumeration — never object names, UIDs, hashes, or messages; guarded by TestMetricLabelCardinalityBounded.

nodes.label: ReplicationPolicy Security Boundary
nodes.rationale: Cluster-scoped, default-deny, allowlist-only with union semantics across matching policies. Evaluated authoritatively on every reconcile rather than at admission, so that policy enforcement is never dependent on webhook availability; supports live revocation (Delete/Retain).

nodes.label: Replication Canonical CR
nodes.rationale: Each annotation request is materialized into an operator-owned Replication object so status and replica inventory live on an object the operator owns, rather than mutating the user's source object.

nodes.label: Annotation-Based Replication Request
nodes.rationale: Annotations on the source Secret/ConfigMap are the whole developer API: zero-friction adoption with no new RBAC for developers.

nodes.label: Pluggable Cluster Discovery (ClusterAPI first)
nodes.rationale: Discovery and transport are interfaces so additional providers and a pull-agent transport arrive as additions, not rewrites.

nodes.label: Minimal-Privilege Spoke Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: The CAPI admin kubeconfig is read uncached and used exactly once per spoke to bootstrap a ServiceAccount scoped to the allowlisted kinds; steady-state traffic uses short-lived self-rotated SA tokens and the spoke rest config carries no static credential. Spoke RBAC is re-narrowed when the allowlist shrinks. This bounds the blast radius of a hub operator compromise.

nodes.label: Drift Detection via Source-Hash
nodes.rationale: Per-cluster metadata-only informers plus an r8r.io/source-hash annotation let the operator detect edited or deleted replicas without ever caching replica payloads on the hub.

nodes.label: Conflict Handling (Fail/Overwrite/Adopt)
nodes.rationale: Fail is the default; Overwrite is policy-gated; Adopt only on content-hash match. Renaming is never automatic, so k8s-r8r cannot silently take over an object it does not manage.

nodes.label: Advisory Admission Webhook
nodes.rationale: CEL-scoped matchConditions with failurePolicy: Ignore. Deliberately advisory-only apply-time feedback so the webhook is never an availability or security dependency; authoritative enforcement stays at reconcile time (design D6).

nodes.label: Alpha Status and Staging-Fleet Trial
nodes.rationale: Architecture is deliberately final while feature surface ships narrow. Coverage is CI-proven, not field-proven: a real ClusterAPI staging fleet trial is surfacing findings faster than CI did, so production use is explicitly discouraged.

nodes.label: Spec-First Workflow Contract (OpenSpec)
nodes.rationale: Behavior changes go through OpenSpec because specs in openspec/specs are the source of truth; docs and the knowledge graph are part of done rather than follow-ups, so implementation and documentation never drift apart.

nodes.label: No Sensitive Data Hard Rule
nodes.rationale: The repository is public, so no real credentials, kubeconfigs, tokens or personal data may ever land in it. Enforced defensively at two layers (pre-push gitleaks hook and CI) rather than by convention; docs and tests use obviously-fake placeholders.

nodes.label: Secret-Safe Telemetry (Hashes Only)
nodes.rationale: No payload data may reach logs, events, conditions or metrics — hashes only. An AST audit test enforces the rule as a ratchet so the guarantee cannot regress silently as new telemetry is added.

nodes.label: AI-Transparency Commit Trailer
nodes.rationale: Commits end with a Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer as a deliberate AI-transparency policy for this public repository — an exception to the usual practice of omitting model co-authors.

nodes.label: Hand-Maintained Webhook Manifests
nodes.rationale: config/webhook/manifests.yaml is maintained by hand because controller-gen cannot express matchConditions; it must be kept in sync with internal/webhook manually.

nodes.label: Developer Certificate of Origin
nodes.rationale: DCO sign-off is used instead of a CLA: every commit carries a Signed-off-by trailer certifying the right to submit under Apache-2.0. Lower friction than a CLA while still establishing provenance; merge commits are exempt.

nodes.label: AI Usage Disclosure Policy
nodes.rationale: The project is developed with substantial AI assistance and says so. Contributors may use AI tools but remain fully responsible for what they submit, and must disclose substantial assistance via a co-author trailer or PR note.

nodes.label: Development Setup and Toolchain
nodes.rationale: make install-hooks is required rather than optional so the gitleaks pre-push scan exists on every contributor machine before the first commit is pushed.

nodes.label: Private Vulnerability Reporting
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, never a public issue, because the operator handles Secrets across cluster fleets and a public report is itself an exposure.

nodes.label: --strip-metadata-keys Flag
nodes.rationale: Extends the stripped-metadata denylist with fleet-specific keys. Additive only — built-in entries cannot be removed — so a fleet cannot weaken the ownership-stripping guarantee. A trailing slash makes an entry a prefix match.

nodes.label: Foreign Ownership Metadata Stripping
nodes.rationale: Replicas previously inherited other controllers' replication and ownership metadata, so a replica of an annotated source became a valid source for that other controller (seeding a second fanout no ReplicationPolicy evaluated), and a replica carrying ArgoCD's tracking label claimed membership in an Application that never declared it, making it a prune candidate. The fix is a denylist scoped to ownership, not an allowlist: all other source metadata still propagates.

nodes.label: Pre-Push Gitleaks Hook
nodes.rationale: Scans only the outgoing commit range (or the whole pushed history for a new branch) so nothing sensitive leaves the machine. Missing gitleaks is a hard failure rather than a silent skip; the documented escape hatch is a one-time --no-verify or a .gitleaks.toml allowlist entry for a false positive.

nodes.label: CI DCO Job
nodes.rationale: Checks a Signed-off-by trailer on every non-merge PR commit. Merge commits are exempt because GitHub's own update-branch merges carry no sign-off; bot-authored (Dependabot) commits are exempt because the bot cannot add the trailer and merging its PR is the maintainer's own certification.

nodes.label: CI Secret Scan Job (gitleaks)
nodes.rationale: Checks out with fetch-depth 0 so gitleaks scans every commit, not just the tip — history is where a leaked secret hides.

nodes.label: CI E2E Job (kind fleet, hub + 2 spokes)
nodes.rationale: Gated behind lint and test so a cheap failure short-circuits the expensive 60-minute fleet run. The suite provisions its own hub + 2 spokes, side-loads the operator image, installs the Helm chart and simulates ClusterAPI inventory; teardown runs with if: always() so a failed run never leaks kind clusters.
nodes.norm_label: ci e2e job (kind fleet, hub + 2 spokes)

nodes.label: govulncheck Vulnerability Scan Workflow
nodes.rationale: Kept out of ci.yml deliberately: the schedule trigger is the point (the Go vulnerability DB moves even when the code does not), a schedule on ci.yml would fire every job weekly or need per-job if: guards, and a separate workflow gives a stable distinct check name for branch protection. The toolchain input tracks the Dockerfile's floating builder tag rather than go.mod's minimum, because go.mod states the module minimum while the shipped binary gets the newest patch — scanning at the minimum over-reports stdlib findings that are never shipped. govulncheck reports only reachable vulnerabilities, which is why a clean run is meaningful rather than a CVE-count ritual.

nodes.label: Release: Publish Container Image
nodes.rationale: Builds multi-arch (amd64/arm64), signs the multi-arch index digest with keyless cosign, and attaches SBOM plus SLSA provenance attestations. Signing by digest rather than tag binds the signature to immutable content; tag selection lives in one step so the :latest / prerelease semantics are expressed in a single place. ANNOTATIONS_LEVELS=index,manifest is what lands OCI annotations on the image index rather than only on per-arch child manifests.

nodes.label: Release: Publish Helm Chart (OCI)
nodes.rationale: Chart version tracks the tag without the v while appVersion is the full tag, so the chart's default image tag (.Chart.AppVersion) resolves to the image published by the same run. Docker login is done in addition to helm registry login because cosign reads ~/.docker/config.json. The pushed manifest digest is parsed out of helm push output so the signature binds to an immutable digest rather than a tag.

nodes.label: Release: Create GitHub Release
nodes.rationale: Runs only after image and chart publish succeed, so a GitHub release never advertises artifacts that were not pushed. Tags containing a hyphen are treated as prereleases.

nodes.label: Dependabot Configuration
nodes.rationale: Weekly updates grouped so a week's bumps arrive as a few reviewable PRs rather than one per module. SHA-pinned uses: entries with a trailing version comment do not opt the repo out of action updates — Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem understands that convention and rewrites both the SHA and the comment.

nodes.label: Pull Request Checklist Template
nodes.rationale: Encodes the definition of done as a checklist: OpenSpec delta for contract changes, unit plus e2e coverage, obsidian and docs updates in the same PR, green lint/tests, no sensitive data or payload telemetry, and AI-assistance disclosure.

nodes.label: Bug Report Issue Form
nodes.rationale: Asks for operator version, hub and spoke Kubernetes versions and the discovery provider because those determine reproducibility, and warns reporters never to paste secret data since the repo is public — the operator itself logs hashes only, but pasted cluster output is not covered by that guarantee.

nodes.label: Feature Request Issue Form
nodes.rationale: States up front that behavior changes go through OpenSpec, so an accepted request becomes a spec change rather than a direct implementation.

nodes.label: Issue Template Router Config
nodes.rationale: Blank issues are disabled and contact links route vulnerabilities to private reporting and questions to Discussions, so the issue tracker stays structured and security reports never land in public.

nodes.label: golangci-lint Configuration
nodes.rationale: Custom module linter logcheck enforces Kubernetes logging conventions; depguard forbids the sort package in favor of slices; goconst ignores tests because repeated literals there are fixture noise rather than missing constants; .claude/worktrees is excluded because parallel agent runs create git worktrees inside the repo and linting them reports every finding twice.

nodes.label: Operator Deployment Template
nodes.rationale: Leader election is always on so replicas greater than one run as hot standbys with exactly one reconciling instance. Hardened pod/container security context (non-root, RuntimeDefault seccomp, read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped). Webhook cert volume and ENABLE_WEBHOOKS=false follow the kubebuilder scaffold convention honored by cmd/main.go.

nodes.label: Chart Install NOTES (Bootstrap Warning)
nodes.rationale: Warns that installing is not a no-op: as soon as a discovered cluster reports control-plane-ready the operator bootstraps a namespace, ServiceAccount and ClusterRole on that spoke, before any policy exists, and the grant follows --allowed-kinds rather than the policies. Operators are told to narrow allowedKinds and read docs/security.md first.

nodes.label: Bootstrap k8s-r8r Operator (change)
nodes.rationale: Greenfield bootstrap of the whole operator. Why: cross-cluster object fanout + pluggable cluster discovery + admin policy gating is an unowned intersection — in-cluster annotation replicators (mittwald/kubernetes-replicator, emberstack/reflector) have no cross-cluster support or policy layer, External Secrets requires an external store, and fleet tools (Fleet, Sveltos, ACM) are heavyweight app-delivery platforms rather than 'replicate this one Secret'.

nodes.label: Ceiling Architecture Principle
nodes.rationale: Governing principle agreed up front: interfaces and data model are final from day one; feature surface ships narrow. Anything known to be needed for scale or hardening later is built into the architecture now, so later features (generic GVKs, ReplicationSet, pull transport, more discovery providers) are additions, never rewrites.

nodes.label: Hub-and-Spoke Replication Architecture
nodes.rationale: Hub holds annotated sources, request controller, canonical Replication CRs, policy gating, CAPI discovery and per-ready-cluster runtimes; spokes hold replicas plus metadata-only watches back to the hub. Credentials flow hub->spoke as SA tokens with narrow RBAC, bootstrapped once from the CAPI kubeconfig.

nodes.label: D1: Annotation Shim over Canonical CRD
nodes.rationale: Annotation is the developer entry point (zero-friction adoption, no new RBAC); every request materializes an operator-owned Replication CR carrying resolved targets, status and replica inventory. Precedent: cert-manager ingress-shim over Certificate. Rejected annotation-only (no status home, no inventory home, no selector future) and CRD-only UX (adoption friction, heavier for the common case). The Replication origin field admits future request kinds such as ReplicationSet.
nodes.norm_label: d1: annotation shim over canonical crd

nodes.label: D2: Push Transport First behind a Transport Interface
nodes.rationale: CAPI already hands over discovery and credentials, so push is dramatically simpler than agent lifecycle plus a hub API. The security cost (hub holds fleet write access) is mitigated by D5 and documented as an explicit threat model. Pull agents remain a future Transport implementation; rejected for v1 because of the larger surface (agent shipping, upgrades, hub API, registration protocol).
nodes.norm_label: d2: push transport first behind a transport interface

nodes.label: D3: Drift Detection via Metadata-Only Filtered Informers
nodes.rationale: One informer per (cluster, replicated GVK) over PartialObjectMetadata, label-filtered to app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: k8s-r8r; drift detected by comparing the r8r.io/source-hash annotation, full object fetched only during reconcile, periodic resync as fallback. Gives event-driven convergence at fleet scale while the hub never caches spoke secret payloads (security and memory in one move). Rejected: polling (slow convergence, O(clusters x replicas x interval) load) and full-object informers (memory, secret data cached on the hub).
nodes.norm_label: d3: drift detection via metadata-only filtered informers

nodes.label: D4: Policy = Default Deny, Allowlists Only, Union
nodes.rationale: No deny rules: deny-precedence logic is the complexity that kills policy engines. Union matches the NetworkPolicy mental model. All matching dimensions must be satisfied by a single policy (no cross-policy dimension mixing). Enforcement is at reconcile time — every reconcile re-evaluates and policy tightening triggers revocation per revocationPolicy; the admission webhook (D6) is UX only.
nodes.norm_label: d4: policy = default deny, allowlists only, union

nodes.label: D5: Minimal-Privilege Spoke Credentials, Bootstrapped Once
nodes.rationale: CAPI kubeconfigs are cluster-admin; using them for steady-state traffic makes the hub a fleet-admin credential store. Instead the kubeconfig is used once per cluster to bootstrap a dedicated namespace, ServiceAccount and narrow RBAC, after which only short-lived rotated SA tokens are used. Hub compromise blast radius drops from 'fleet admin' to 'write allowlisted kinds in allowlisted namespaces'. Built in v1 because retrofitting credential minimization never happens in practice.
nodes.norm_label: d5: minimal-privilege spoke credentials, bootstrapped once

nodes.label: D6: Advisory Webhook, Controller Authoritative
nodes.rationale: failurePolicy: Fail would make operator downtime block all secret writes cluster-wide, which is unacceptable. The webhook is therefore strictly UX (apply-time error messages), scoped via CEL matchConditions to annotated objects only, and its absence can never cause unauthorized replication because the controller re-checks policy on every reconcile. This split must be stated in the security docs.

nodes.label: D7: Conflict Policy Fail | Overwrite | Adopt
nodes.rationale: Overwrite is weaponizable (replace a victim cluster's existing secret), so it is policy-gated and request-explicit. Adopt only on content-hash equality. Automatic prefix/suffix renaming rejected because consumers mount secrets by name and a silent rename breaks workloads with no error surfaced anywhere; an explicit r8r.io/target-name override exists for deliberate, git-visible renames.
nodes.norm_label: d7: conflict policy fail | overwrite | adopt

nodes.label: D9: Workqueue Keyed (source, targetCluster)
nodes.rationale: Per-target keys mean one slow or unreachable cluster backs off independently without blocking the rest of the fanout, and future sharding-by-cluster requires no re-keying.

nodes.label: Hub Blast Radius Risk
nodes.rationale: The hub is a high-value target because it can write secrets fleet-wide. Mitigations: D5 narrow SAs, kubeconfig Secrets isolated in a dedicated namespace with tight RBAC, a documented threat model, and audit-friendly events. Related accepted risks: watch-per-cluster-per-GVK egress load (metadata-only watches are cheap, sharding path prepared via D9), finalizers blocking deletion when spokes are unreachable (bounded retries plus ClusterGone release), CEL matchConditions requiring Kubernetes >= 1.30, immutable-field conflicts under Adopt/Overwrite, union-only policy coarseness, and the unverified r8r.io domain assumption.

nodes.label: Replication CRD (canonical object)
nodes.rationale: Operator-owned canonical object per source in group r8r.io/v1alpha1, carrying resolved targets, status summary/conditions, replica inventory and origin kind. It is the single home for status and inventory that annotations alone cannot provide.

nodes.label: ReplicationPolicy CRD
nodes.rationale: Cluster-scoped CRD that is the security boundary: default deny, allowlist-only, union semantics across policies, admin-scoped RBAC.

nodes.label: ReplicationSet CRD (future selector-based requests)
nodes.rationale: Explicit non-goal of the bootstrap change; the canonical Replication layer is built ready for it so a selector-based request CRD can materialize the same Replication objects without touching engine, policy or status contracts.

nodes.label: Transport Interface
nodes.rationale: Pluggable seam for how replicas reach spokes. v1 ships only the push implementation using SA-token clients from cluster runtimes; the pull-agent slot exists but is deliberately unfilled.

nodes.label: Discovery Provider Interface
nodes.rationale: Pluggable seam turning fleet-management systems into replication target inventory; ClusterAPI is the first and only v1 provider. Adding providers (Fleet, Rancher, static kubeconfig list, cloud APIs) must not require changes to the engine, policy or request layers.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Implementation Task Plan
nodes.rationale: Ten completed work streams: scaffold and CI, CRD APIs, policy engine, request controller (annotation shim), discovery layer, replication engine, admission webhook, observability and HA, packaging and docs (including a threat model documenting D5/D6 reasoning), and multi-kind-cluster e2e validation.

nodes.label: Tag-Triggered Release Workflow
nodes.rationale: Push of a v* tag is the single source of truth: image tag = <tag>, chart version = <tag without v>, chart appVersion = <tag>, so the chart's default image tag (.Chart.AppVersion) always resolves to the image published by the same run.

nodes.label: :latest Tag Gating on Non-Prerelease Semver
nodes.rationale: Only tags without a '-' also push :latest, so prereleases such as v0.2.0-alpha.1 can never move the latest pointer that unpinned users follow. The GitHub release is likewise marked prerelease when the tag contains '-'.

nodes.label: GHCR Publishing with GITHUB_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: Publish to ghcr.io using GITHUB_TOKEN with packages: write so no extra secrets are needed; the chart goes to oci://ghcr.io/moeritze/charts so image and chart packages do not collide. Known trade-offs: ghcr packages default to private on first publish (one-time manual visibility flip, documented in docs/releasing.md) and multi-arch arm64 builds under QEMU are slow but acceptable at tag-only cadence.

nodes.label: SHA-Pinned Actions and Minimal Permissions
nodes.rationale: Repo CI style: actions pinned to commit SHAs, top-level permissions: {} with per-job grants (packages: write for publish jobs, contents: write for the release job). docker/* SHAs were resolved from the GitHub API at authoring time; actions/checkout reuses the SHA already pinned in ci.yml.

nodes.label: GitHub Release via gh CLI
nodes.rationale: Use `gh release create --generate-notes` instead of a third-party release action: one fewer supply-chain pin, and gh (like helm) is preinstalled on runners.

nodes.label: Kind-Allowlist-Derived Spoke RBAC Scope
nodes.rationale: parseAllowedKinds turns the --allowed-kinds flag (default secrets,configmaps) into the cluster.RBACScope handed to the spoke wirer. The grant is get,list,watch,create,update,patch,delete on each allowlisted resource with no resourceNames and no namespace restriction, bound cluster-wide via a ClusterRoleBinding, plus get,create,patch on namespaces. Re-narrowing on an allowlist shrink already works because UpdateRBAC replaces ClusterRole rules wholesale and a flag change restarts the pod, after which discovery re-emits Register for every cluster.

nodes.label: Policy-Derived Scoping Gap (issue #29)
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the tree reads a ReplicationPolicy to build the spoke scope, so a hub whose only policy permits Secret still grants cluster-wide ConfigMap delete on every discovered spoke, and the grant exists from install time before any policy is authored. Closing it is a 10-14h implementation that first needs a decision on whether the provider admin credential stays one-shot. Deferred and tracked as issue #29.

nodes.label: RBACScope (bootstrap seam)
nodes.rationale: The struct in internal/cluster/bootstrap.go describing what the spoke ClusterRole grants. Named in the spec as the stable seam for both deferred narrowings (policy-derived scoping and per-namespace Roles), and the place a future implementer looks first — hence the doc comment extension in this change.

nodes.label: Restate the Requirement Rather Than Weaken It
nodes.rationale: Leaving the aspirational wording plus a caveat was rejected: a SHALL that nothing implements and nothing tests is indistinguishable from a lie in an audit, and the spec is meant to be the source of truth for what the operator does today. The aspiration survives as an explicit deferral with an issue reference, which is honest about both current state and intent. Accepted cost: the spec temporarily encodes a weaker guarantee.
nodes.norm_label: restate the requirement rather than weaken it

nodes.label: Factual Blast-Radius Correction
nodes.rationale: Read-and-delete on every Secret in every namespace of every spoke (kube-system, cert-manager, argocd, flux-system included) is not meaningfully bounded away from fleet admin, so the old 'bounded and auditable' claim overstated the reduction. What stays true is that this is not a privilege escalation — the hub already holds CAPI admin kubeconfigs. The gap defeats the reduction D5 promises, while D5's genuine wins (no static credential in the spoke rest config, short-lived rotated tokens, admin kubeconfig touched once per bootstrap) are unaffected. Disclosing this in a public repo is framed as a documented alpha limitation with a tracking issue, not an exploit path.

nodes.label: Self-Narrowing Spoke ServiceAccount (proposed alternative)
nodes.source_location: Decisions / Why policy-derived scoping is deferred
nodes.rationale: The naive fix — watch ReplicationPolicy, recompute the scope, call UpdateRBAC — is worse than the bug: widening a spoke grant needs a credential that can escalate, so the hub would hold the provider admin kubeconfig for routine policy edits, converting an auditable rare event into a routine one and undermining D5 more than the over-broad grant does. The promising alternative is to grant the spoke SA get,update on its own ClusterRole by resourceNames, so RBAC escalation-prevention makes widening structurally impossible while narrowing needs no admin credential and widening stays a bootstrap-class event. Belongs in its own change with its own review.
